items.subject: Known residue: one backend reachable through SEVERAL transports yields one delta entry carrying one transport’s pattern, so an autonomous fail-closed exclusion drops only that route. Tracked in docs/backlog.md.
items.title: Backend-identity Stage 5 shipped, but two docs still describe its residue as open — and they point at each other
items.eli5: Two documents describe a limitation that the code no longer has. The dispatch worker-model spec carries a warning box saying that when one vendor can be reached over several different routes, an automatic "rule this backend out" write only rules out the single route it happened to record — leaving the other routes still usable. That was true once. It is not true now: the code was changed (commit c3567b27, already in the current tree) so the automatic write rules out the vendor itself rather than one route, which covers every route at once. The spec’s sibling document, backend-identity-axes.md, already states the corrected behaviour, so the two specs in the same cluster now contradict each other. Separately, the backlog lists this same work as "Stage 5" under an "Open remainder" heading, phrased as future work that still needs a review attestation — and the spec’s warning box says the residue is "Tracked in docs/backlog.md", which is that very bullet. That is why this is one decision and not two: deleting only the backlog bullet would leave the spec pointing at something that no longer exists, and deleting only the spec note would leave the backlog claiming work that is done. One caveat worth knowing before you answer: the first half of the warning is still literally true — there really is only one delta entry per backend, because the code deliberately keeps the first route it sees. It is the consequence drawn from that fact that is now wrong. So "just delete it" and "rewrite it to say what actually remains" are both defensible, which is why this is your call rather than an automatic fix.
items.question: Stage 5 (fail-closed autonomous write emits the service axis) shipped in c3567b27. Do you want the spec’s "Known residue" warning and the backlog’s "Stage 5" bullet both deleted, or rewritten to state the narrower residual that genuinely remains (one delta entry per backend, first-writer-wins) without the refuted consequence?

options.label: Delete both
options.answer: Delete the "Known residue" paragraph from spec/unified-dispatch-worker-model.md and the "Stage 5" bullet from docs/backlog/forward-tracks.md. The work shipped; a shipped-status note is status-noise and first-writer-wins is already described elsewhere in the spec.

options.label: Rewrite both to the real residual
options.answer: Keep a note in the spec but rewrite it: state that one backend yields one delta entry (first-writer-wins) and that the autonomous fail-closed write emits the service axis so this does not narrow the exclusion. Delete the backlog Stage 5 bullet, since the work is done and the durable fact now lives in the spec.

options.label: Spec only, keep the backlog bullet
options.answer: Fix the spec’s residue paragraph and leave the backlog Stage 5 bullet alone — there is remaining work under that entry that the bullet is tracking.

evidence: c3567b27 "backend-identity migration stage 5 — fail-closed autonomous write emits service: axis" is an ancestor of HEAD (git merge-base --is-ancestor confirmed) and touched exactly the files the backlog bullet names: src/audit/orchestrator/intakeExecutors.ts, src/shared/providers/identity.ts, src/shared/providers/sharedProviderConfirmation.ts.
serviceExclusionPattern(modelId, service) in src/shared/providers/identity.ts always returns a `service:`-prefixed pattern and can never return null.
src/shared/providers/sharedProviderConfirmation.ts sets service_exclusion_pattern unconditionally inside record(), for every recorded backend.
src/audit/orchestrator/intakeExecutors.ts consumes it preferentially in the autonomous fail-closed write: `b.service_exclusion_pattern ?? b.exclusion_pattern`.

The sibling spec spec/backend-identity-axes.md states the corrected fact outright: "The autonomous fail-closed write emits the service axis, because that is the axis that does not decay." The two specs in one cluster disagree, and the code matches the axes doc.

STILL TRUE, and why this is not a plain deletion: record() keeps `if (reachNow.has(identity)) return;` — first-writer-wins, so there genuinely is one delta entry per backend identity. Only the consequence ("drops only that route") is refuted.

The spec paragraph says the residue is "Tracked in docs/backlog.md"; the tracking bullet is docs/backlog/forward-tracks.md "Stage 5", which sits under "Open remainder:" and reads as unstarted work ("Touches intakeExecutors.ts → loop-core, attestation required").
Reviewer lane surfaced the spec half; an independent adversary lane agreed on both sub-claims and separately flagged the backlog Stage 5 bullet. Verified again by hand against HEAD ccb530d7.

items.subject: The last approved build — guard reach as declared data (ec64d159) — shipped in 3cd3dbc1: scripts/guard-reach-data.mjs registers every guard, its wiring and its scanned set (uncovered halves stated as data); check:guard-reach reconciles it in verify:checks plus an unconditional pre-commit leg.
items.title: HANDOFF re-narrates a shipped mechanism that CLAUDE.md already owns — changelog creep, or legitimate current state?
items.eli5: The handoff document has a passage describing the guard-reach mechanism that shipped a few commits ago: which script holds the registry, what it records, and which gates run it. The same mechanism is already described durably in CLAUDE.md, in its "Durable traps are MECHANICALLY enforced" paragraph. So the description now exists in two places, and the two will drift apart over time — the repo’s own documentation philosophy calls that out as "one home per concept". The handoff copy additionally narrates the work as completed and cites two commit hashes, which is the shape its own header explicitly warns against: that header says this section "had twice grown into version-by-version narration, which is the changelog creep this doc’s own header forbids". The reason this is a question rather than an automatic edit is that HANDOFF is the one document in this repo that is *supposed* to hold current state and sequencing — saying "the last approved determination landed, here is where" is arguably exactly its job, not creep. Deciding which of those two readings applies is a judgment about what the handoff is for, so the routine will not make it alone.
items.question: Does this passage count as the changelog creep HANDOFF’s own header forbids — trim it to a pointer at CLAUDE.md and the ledger — or is naming the last landed determination legitimate current-state sequencing that should stay?

options.label: Trim to a pointer
options.answer: Trim it. HANDOFF should say the last determination landed and point at the decisions ledger; the mechanism description belongs only in CLAUDE.md, which already has it. Drop the commit hashes and the re-description.

options.label: Keep — this is current state, not creep
options.answer: Keep it. Naming the last approved determination and where it landed is what HANDOFF is for, and the commit refs are how the next agent orients. The CLAUDE.md paragraph is the durable rule; this is the sequencing view.

options.label: Keep the fact, drop the mechanism restatement
options.answer: Keep the sentence naming ec64d159 as landed in 3cd3dbc1, but delete the trailing re-description of what guard-reach-data.mjs does and which gates run it — that half is the duplicated part.

evidence: CLAUDE.md already carries the same mechanism in its "Durable traps are MECHANICALLY enforced" paragraph: "Guard wiring + reach are DECLARED DATA … scripts/guard-reach-data.mjs registers every guard … npm run check:guard-reach … reconciles the registry against the tracked tree."
docs/HANDOFF.md’s own header states the section "had twice grown into version-by-version narration, which is the changelog creep this doc’s own header forbids".
docs/documentation-philosophy.md forbids changelog/progress creep and states one home per concept.
Countervailing: the doc-manifest routes docs/HANDOFF.md as the sanctioned sequencing/current-state view, so a current-state claim there is not automatically status-noise.
Both commits are real and are ancestors of HEAD: 3cd3dbc1 landed the registry; 83c56e0d recorded ec64d159 DONE in the determinations ledger.
Reviewer lane raised this at medium confidence, explicitly as a judgment call rather than a factual error. No auto-apply was attempted.

items.subject: The backlog-triage lane reports every provider error as finish_reason=undefined, retries nothing, and adds errored ids to its own resume set.
items.title: Leg 2 has failed two nights running on a masked rate limit — the lane throws away the error that names its own retry-after
items.eli5: Leg 2 of this routine checks every backlog entry against the code to find entries whose work already shipped. It does that through a helper script that asks a cheap model to classify one entry at a time. Tonight that script failed on 94 of 106 entries, and every single failure recorded the same message: "finish_reason=undefined". That message says nothing, so the natural reading is that the model is broken — which is why three different models were tried, each converting only a handful more entries. Adding one line to print the actual response body gave the real answer immediately: the provider was returning a plain rate-limit error stating its own limit (8000 tokens per minute), how much was used, and exactly how long to wait ("Please try again in 20.4525s"). The script throws all of that away, because it only looks for a field that a rate-limit response does not contain. It also never waits and retries. And a third problem hides the first two: when the script resumes, it marks every previously-seen entry as done — including the failed ones — so simply re-running it retries nothing and exits successfully, which looks like the run completed. The fix does not need new machinery: this repo already has a shared quota-error parser that reads exactly these retry-after fields. The script hand-rolls a worse version of something it could import.
items.question: Approve fixing the triage lane to surface the provider’s real error, honour the stated retry-after through the existing shared quota error parser, and stop adding errored ids to the resume set?

options.label: Approve all three fixes
options.answer: Approve. Surface the response body’s error.message and HTTP status instead of finish_reason; classify through src/shared/quota/errorParsing.ts and wait the stated retry-after before retrying the same entry, with a per-entry attempt cap after which the real error is recorded; and only add ids without an error to the resume set.

options.label: Surface the error only, no retry logic
options.answer: Just surface the real error and fix the resume set. Do not add retry/backoff to this script — an operator re-running it with the error visible is enough, and a retry loop is more machinery than a triage helper needs.

options.label: Retire the script, route leg 2 differently
options.answer: Do not fix it. Leg 2 should not depend on a rate-limited free lane at all — route the shipped-detection pass through a different mechanism and retire this script.

evidence: Instrumenting the throw revealed the masked body verbatim: {"error":{"message":"Rate limit reached for model `openai/gpt-oss-120b` … on tokens per minute (TPM): Limit 8000, Used 5818, Requested 4909. Please try again in 20.4525s …","type":"tokens","code":"rate_limit_exceeded"}}.

scripts/shared/triage-backlog.mjs throws `finish_reason=${c?.finish_reason}` where c is r.choices?.[0]; a provider error body has no choices array, so c is undefined and the message carries no information. The response’s error.message is discarded.

Line 178: `done.add(rec.id)` runs before the error check, and the queue is `entries.filter(e => !done.has(e.id))` — so errored rows ARE skipped on re-run. This contradicts the script’s own line-21 comment, "Errored rows are NOT skipped". Tonight’s coverage only advanced because the errored rows were stripped from the JSONL by hand between passes.

The lane is NOT incapable: with the same full schema and a short system prompt, groq/openai/gpt-oss-120b classified a previously-failing 139-character entry correctly on the first attempt. The 8000 TPM ceiling is the whole constraint.

Ruled out by measurement, not assumption: payload size is not the discriminator (smallest failing entry was 139 chars; failed-vs-succeeded length medians were 1409 vs 1432), and concurrency is not either (TRIAGE_CONCURRENCY=1 still errored on 80 of 106).

The repo already owns the fix: src/shared/quota/errorParsing.ts reads retry_after_ms, retry-after, Retry-After and retry_after and normalises to milliseconds, alongside a whole src/shared/quota/errorParsers/ directory.

Recurrence, four records on four dates: the 2026-07-29 nightly recorded leg 2 in its skipped list after the Codex lane returned unfalsifiable leads; tonight 78–94 entries were lost to this masked 429; docs/backlog/durable-traps.md already warns "the offload lane degrades on TWO independent axes — payload SIZE and CONCURRENCY — and both look like model incapacity"; and project memory already carries offload-lane-failures-are-usually-the-caller. The trap is written down twice and still cost two nights.

THIRD defect in the same script, and it bit this run live: every record is keyed `<file>#<ordinal position>`, a position in a file that leg 2 exists to DELETE entries from. After a shipped entry was removed from open-bugs.md this run, every already-classified row from that ordinal onward named a different entry and the resume set would have skipped them as done; the in-flight artifact was discarded and the pass restarted. The repo already keys on content elsewhere for exactly this reason (itemHash over normalized text in the doc-review scope ledger; subjectKey in scripts/nightly/items.mjs).
Full proposal with the patch shape and the false-positive analysis: .audit-tools/nightly/proposals/P5-triage-lane-masks-429/PROPOSAL.md

IF THIS IS DECLINED, the trap still needs a durable home: the "re-running the script retries nothing and exits 0" behaviour is a standing gotcha for anyone re-running it regardless of whether the fix lands, and it currently exists only in this item and its proposal (both under .audit-tools/, which is untracked). Declining means filing it as an entry in docs/backlog/durable-traps.md in the same pass.

items.subject: The verify:checks step list is restated in prose in docs/audit-pkg/release.md and .claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md, hand-maintained against package.json.
items.title: The gate step list is hand-copied into two docs and drifted on two consecutive nights — generate it, the way the README philosophy block already is
items.eli5: The list of checks that make up the release gate lives for real in package.json, as the verify:checks script. It is also written out in prose in two other places: the release guide and the ship skill. Those two copies are maintained by hand, which means every time a new check is added to the gate, both copies silently become wrong and nothing fails — the error only surfaces when a human happens to compare them. That has now happened on two nights in a row. Last night this routine added a missing check:doc-links row to the release guide and missing doc-links and nightly-routine-prompt rows to the ship skill, and recorded that the ship skill "now matches package.json in exact order". Tonight both were stale again, because a new check landed in between. This repo has already solved this exact problem once: the README’s philosophy section used to be a hand-maintained restatement, and CLAUDE.md describes retiring that as replacing "a drift test made of memory, which is the thing this project bans" — it is now generated and parity-gated. The proposal is to do the same here: render both lists from package.json through a small data module that supplies each step’s human-readable gloss, and add a parity gate so a hand-edited list fails the build.
items.question: Approve generating the verify:checks / verify:release step enumerations from package.json with a parity gate, the same pattern as check:philosophy-brief and check:doc-manifest?

options.label: Approve — generate both, with a gloss data module
options.answer: Approve. Add marker-delimited generated blocks to both docs, render from package.json step order through a data module mapping step to its human gloss (same shape as scripts/doc-manifest-data.mjs), and gate byte parity with a check script in verify:checks supporting --write. A gate step with no gloss is a build failure.

options.label: Gate only — fail on drift, keep the prose hand-written
options.answer: Do not generate the prose. Just add a check that fails when a verify:checks step is named in package.json but appears in neither doc’s list, and leave the wording to a human.

options.label: Only the machine-readable list, drop the glosses
options.answer: Generate a bare step list from package.json in both docs and drop the per-step human glosses — the script names are self-explanatory enough and a gloss table is more to maintain.

options.label: Leave it — the nightly catching it is fine
options.answer: Leave it as is. The nightly doc review catches the drift within a day, and that is a cheap enough backstop for a prose list that nothing executes.

evidence: package.json verify:checks is the single source of truth and currently has 23 steps, with check:guard-reach third, between check:version-gates and check:loop-core-patterns.

Tonight, both prose lists omitted check:guard-reach entirely — confirmed by a reviewer lane, an independent adversary lane, and a direct comparison against package.json. Both were fixed as leg-1 stale-factual edits this run.

Last night’s applied list recorded the same class of fix twice: "docs/audit-pkg/release.md — the verify:release enumeration gained the missing check:doc-links row" and ".claude/skills/ship/SKILL.md — the verify:checks enumeration gained the missing doc-links and nightly-routine-prompt rows; it now matches package.json in exact order."
Four omissions across two files on two consecutive nights. check:guard-reach landed in 3cd3dbc1, a commit with no reason to know two prose restatements existed.

The precedent is in-repo and explicit: CLAUDE.md’s "One brief, two consumers — never a second copy of the philosophy" describes the README philosophy block as previously "a hand-maintained restatement kept honest by an instruction to remember to update it — a drift test made of memory, which is the thing this project bans". It is now generated and gated by check:philosophy-brief in verify:release.

Two comparable generators already exist and are not known false-failure sources: check:philosophy-brief and check:doc-manifest (the latter rendering from scripts/doc-manifest-data.mjs, the gloss-data shape this proposal reuses).

Design wrinkle for the owner: the two docs render the same list differently — release.md as glossed bullets, ship/SKILL.md as a "+"-joined inline sentence — so this is one source with two render shapes.
Full proposal: .audit-tools/nightly/proposals/P6-gate-enumeration-generated/PROPOSAL.md

items.subject: evaluateProbes maps ENOENT to state absent, so a probe naming a path that never existed is indistinguishable from a probe whose code vanished, and all-absent means resolved.
items.title: A probe path that does not exist reads exactly like a premise that vanished — 44% of tonight’s leg-2 probes, and 20 of its 27 "already done" stamps
items.eli5: Backlog and nightly items carry "premise probes": a file plus a literal string quoted from it, so the tool can mechanically check whether the thing an item complains about is still in the code. If every quoted string has disappeared, the item is treated as done and closed automatically. The bug is in how "disappeared" is decided. The checker tries to read the file; if the file is not there at all, it records the same result as if the file were there and simply no longer contained the text. Those are completely different facts — the second means the work shipped, the first means somebody wrote the path wrong — and collapsing them turns a typo into the strongest possible claim, "this is already finished". This is not hypothetical. Tonight’s leg-2 pass asks a model to emit those probes, and that model cannot see the repository, so it writes bare filenames like "serve.mjs" instead of "scripts/nightly/serve.mjs". Of the probes it produced, 44% named a path that does not resolve, and 20 of the 27 rows stamped "premise gone" rest on at least one of them. Every one of those files genuinely exists, just at a real path. There is already a guard for this on the other consumer — the nightly items file refuses to save an item whose probes do not currently pass — but the backlog-triage path has no such check, so the bad probes there become the most confident verdict in the file, and that verdict is the input to deleting backlog entries. The fix is to stop collapsing the two absences: report "file missing" separately from "text missing", and never let a missing file contribute to an automatic close.
items.question: Approve splitting probe absence into "file not found" versus "fragment not found" in evaluateProbes, so only a genuine fragment-absence can auto-close an item, and a malformed probe degrades to no-signal instead of to "shipped"?

options.label: Approve — split the states, no-such-path never closes
options.answer: Approve. Split evaluateProbes into present / absent (file read, fragment gone) / no-such-path (ENOENT) / error. Only all-absent may yield resolved, so a no-such-path can never contribute to an auto-close on either consumer. writeOpenItems keeps refusing non-present probes but reports a bad path as a bad path; triage-backlog stamps an all-bad-path row as unprobed rather than gone.

options.label: Approve, and also resolve bare filenames
options.answer: Approve the state split, and additionally have the triage script resolve a bare filename against the tracked file list, accepting it when the match is unambiguous — since the model reliably emits bare filenames and they each resolve uniquely.

options.label: Fix the triage caller only
options.answer: Leave evaluateProbes alone and fix only the triage script: validate that each probe path names a tracked file before trusting an absence. The nightly path is already protected by the creation-time refusal.

options.label: Leave it — the stamp is advisory anyway
options.answer: Leave it. Triage output is explicitly advisory and must be verified against HEAD before acting, so a noisy premise stamp is tolerable and the reader is already told not to trust it.

evidence: scripts/nightly/items.mjs, evaluateProbes: `state = err && err.code === 'ENOENT' ? 'absent' : 'error';` — a missing file scores the same as a present file missing the fragment. Two lines later, `const status = evaluated.every((p) => p.state === 'absent') ? 'resolved' : 'open';` turns all-absent into resolved.

Measured over tonight’s classified triage rows: 95 probes emitted, 42 (44%) naming a path that does not resolve; 20 of 35 probed rows (57%) carry at least one; and of the 27 rows stamped gone/partial, 20 (74%) rest on at least one unresolvable path.

Reproduced concretely — open-bugs#36 probes `proxyCatalog.ts`, open-bugs#45 probes `providerConfirmationStep.ts`, open-bugs#1 probes `serve.mjs`. None exists at the repo root; each exists exactly once in the tracked tree at a real path (verified with git ls-files). So each read throws ENOENT, scores absent, and the row is stamped gone.

The cause is structural, not a bad model day: triage-backlog.mjs tells the model to emit "the repo-relative path the entry names" while the model has NO repo access, so a bare filename is the expected output.

The guard exists but only on the other consumer: writeOpenItems refuses any probe that is not `present` at creation, so nightly items are protected; triage-backlog.mjs calls the same evaluator through premiseStamp with no refusal at all, and its stamp feeds leg 2’s deletion decisions.
This is the shape CLAUDE.md names: "A trap enforced only partly is NOT deletable — state the uncovered half outright, or the covered half reads as a close."

Secondary consequence on the protected path: because the two absences are indistinguishable, a later RENAME sends every probe absent and partitionBySettled auto-closes the item as resolved without surfacing it. The item contract concedes this ("a rename mis-closes") only because the evaluator cannot tell the cases apart — the split retires the concession.
Consequence for this run, stated so it is not mistaken for a clean result: NO backlog entry was deleted on the strength of a premise:gone stamp, because the stamp is not trustworthy evidence.
Full proposal: .audit-tools/nightly/proposals/P7-probe-absence-conflates-bad-path/PROPOSAL.md
